info.title: Korsi plugin API
info.description:
``/plugin/v1`` -- the plugin plane: what an installed plugin calls (section 9).

**Its own plane, with its own contract.** ``/api/v1`` changes with every release of the web app and
is not a promise to anybody outside this repository; this plane is versioned, documented in its own
OpenAPI (``/plugin/v1/openapi.json``) and kept compatible for a major version. It is also the only
place a plugin can write: its own records, its proposals, its sources and its wallet.

**Reading Korsi is MCP's.** A plugin reads cases, people, meetings, documents, the calendar and
memory through Korsi's MCP server with the same credential, and sees exactly the tools its scopes
cover (section 9, "MCP first"). This plane serves the reads only a plugin needs: who it is, its own
records, the colleagues it may address, and its event stream.

**Who is calling.** Either the installation's own machine user, a ZITADEL token whose roles include
``plugin_installation``, resolved with the installation's scopes as a ceiling -- or a person through
a sealed handle (:mod:`.handles`): the person's own token, verified again here, resolved with the
same ceiling, and refused unless the person is still among those the installation is shown to. A
token that is neither (a person's ordinary token, an agent's) is refused: nothing on this plane is
for anybody but a plugin.

**Budgets.** Every route spends one request from one of the installation's four budgets -- reads,
writes, sources, proposals (:mod:`.limits`) -- before it opens a session, and past one it is
answered ``429`` with ``Retry-After``.

Colleague.title: Colleague
Colleague.description:
One person in this tenant, as a picker or a label needs them.

The shape every "who is this" question in the product resolves to. It exists because four
domains were each building it from ``app_user`` joined to ``tenant_member``, and a fifth was
about to: an owner picker in Operations, a voice picker in Meetings, an allocation picker in
Commerce, and actor labels in analysis views. Four copies of one query is four chances to
forget the status filter, and one of them had.

``label`` is resolved server-side rather than sent as a name plus an email for the client to
choose between. Which one to show is one decision -- display name, or the address when nobody
has set one -- and making it here is what stops two screens showing the same person
differently.

``status`` is carried rather than filtered out, because the two questions this answers want
opposite things. A picker offers only active members: a removed colleague must not be
assignable. A label must resolve for anybody, including somebody who has left, or a case they
used to own loses its history the day their account closes.

LocalizedText.title: LocalizedText
LocalizedText.description:
A name or a sentence in the languages Korsi ships. At least one is required.

Persian first, because it is the default language of the product; any one is accepted so a
publisher writing in one language is not refused, and the store falls back through
:meth:`pick`.

MembershipStatus.title: MembershipStatus
MembershipStatus.description:
Whether a user may act inside a tenant.

``REMOVED`` rather than deleting the row: membership history is what makes an
audit entry from last year legible, and re-adding somebody must not silently
revive whatever their old roles were.
